verdict.rationale: OpenTofu's automations are plain-text configuration files that its docs explicitly describe as versionable like any other code (opentofu-gh-2, opentofu-docs-28, opentofu-docs-16). Review is well covered: `tofu plan` previews changes, speculative plans are meant for code review, and saved plans via `-out` let the reviewed plan be the one that gets applied (opentofu-docs-3, opentofu-docs-4, opentofu-docs-21). No evidence shows a native rollback capability; rollback would depend on reverting in an external VCS and re-applying, which is a user-side workaround. Versioning itself also relies on external source control rather than a built-in history. missing for 10: native rollback or state-revert capability, built-in version history (rather than external VCS), independent hands-on corroboration of a review/rollback workflow.
